paragraphs: The F15-generation X5 xDrive35i and xDrive40i are effectively the same vehicle with a running engine change. Earlier cars use the N55 — a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six that BMW introduced in 2009 and fitted across a wide range of models. From around the mid-cycle update, the xDrive35i became the xDrive40i with the B58 engine, a newer closed-deck design that's a genuine successor to the N55, not just a revision. Both are well-regarded petrol straight-sixes, and both are supported by our rebuild service.
about.boldParagraph: The X5 xDrive35i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol fitted to the X5 xDrive35i from 2013 to around the facelift period. Generally well-regarded — no specific failure pattern is considered a hero hook for this engine. We replace timing chain, bearings and gaskets as standard on every N55 rebuild.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol, the successor to the N55, fitted to the xDrive40i from around the 2018 model year. No significant known issues confirmed for this application. We service it to the same standard as our other X5 rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the xDrive35i and xDrive40i overlap across the same F15 generation but use two different engine codes, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N55 part will work on a B58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N55 or B58) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic X5 quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
